x: Open Vanilla is a free, community-run home for classic Vanilla. You can play on the official Vanilla Remastered realm (Vanilla with careful quality-of-life additions), play solo offline with bots, or host your own realm for friends. It's built on the open-source benilla client and runs in your browser or on Windows. Note: Open Vanilla is a fan project. It isn't affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard, it sells nothing, and it never ships Blizzard's game files: you use a copy of Vanilla Client v1.3 you obtain yourself.

Open play.openvanilla.app . Press Sign in with Discord , or Play as guest to try it first. Create a character and play. The first load downloads game data; after that it loads from your disk. Details: Playing in the browser .

Download the launcher from the home page ( Desktop Client ): OpenVanilla-Setup-<version>.exe is the recommended installer, or the zip for a portable copy. Start it. On Home , the bar above PLAY says what's missing; pressing PLAY fixes it: it downloads Vanilla Client v1.3 or lets you pick the folder you already have. Press PLAY . The first time, it signs you in with Discord. Details: The launcher . Note: The launcher isn't code-signed yet, so Windows may say "Unknown publisher" or show SmartScreen. Choose More info → Run anyway , or check the file against the checksums on the release page first

Sign in with Discord is the one button for new and returning players: the first time, it creates your realm account and adds you to the Open Vanilla Discord. Open Vanilla never sees your Discord password or messages. Guests get a real account tied to that device (kept for 30 days of inactivity). Press Save your heroes — link Discord in game to keep your characters for good. Accounts live on each realm: a community realm has its own accounts and its own website. Staff will never ask for your password.

t: What you need: Vanilla Client v1.3
x: The desktop game needs your own copy of Vanilla Client v1.3 (English, build 5875). The launcher's game setup page either downloads one ( Download & install , a few GB, resumable) or checks a folder you already have ( Select existing folder ). It never changes the game's files. More on clients.html and in The launcher .
New to the interface? In-game features , then the command cheat sheet . Want friends? Realms and friends , Community . Want to build? Edit your own game , Connect an AI , Publish to the Workshop .

The browser client needs WebGPU . Current desktop Chrome and Edge have it; other browsers vary. If the page reports "no WebGPU adapter", update your browser or graphics driver, or use the launcher instead. A broadband connection helps for the first load.

The first visit downloads the game data the realm streams to you, and keeps it on your disk. The next visit loads from disk and only fetches what changed. The page asks your browser to keep this storage (Firefox shows a prompt; Chrome doesn't), so your keybinds, macros and addon settings survive too. Note: Browser settings are stored in that browser only. A different browser or device starts fresh.

Your first trip into the world uses lite textures (about a quarter of the texture data) so you're playing sooner. After two minutes in the world the page switches to full textures on your next load. The dock's Textures button cycles auto / lite / full ; changes apply on the next load.

The handle at the top centre opens the dock: account, password, notifications (bell), full screen and sign out. Full screen captures Escape, Tab and W, so Ctrl+W won't close the tab by accident. ♫ Listening (in the ☰ menu) shares what you're listening to on your Persona, if you want: see the website chapter . If the realm is full, slow or down, a note offers Play Solo on your PC instead.

The launcher checks for updates by itself and ignores anything that isn't signed by Open Vanilla's release key or is older than what you have. Updates download quietly in the background ("Downloading update 42%"), are checked against their fingerprint, and then a gold UPDATE READY · RESTART button appears above PLAY. Updating replaces only program files: your addons, settings, realms and screenshots are never touched. If an update fails, it says so and tries again next time (details in Logs\update.log ).

Your data folder is %LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenVanilla for the installer (an install from before the rename keeps its older data folder), or the folder beside OpenVanilla.exe for the zip. In the launcher, Realms → Realm browser shows the live directory, filterable by type, template and free room, plus your favourites and recent realms. Realms come in groups: Group Meaning Verified realms · Official Run by Open Vanilla Verified realms · Vetted Checked by the maintainers Community P2P realms Hosted by players; not vetted, play at your own risk The website's realm list shows the same directory.

Realms → My servers → Add a server : name, host or IP, port (default 3724 ), the realm's website (optional) and which client to use. Each row shows its ping, with Select , Website and Remove . The Community list has hand-picked servers with a Play here button. Using a stock client without the launcher? Put set realmlist <address> in the client's realmlist.wtf .

A friend hosting a realm can send you an invite link. Paste it in the Invite link box and press Join invite , or just click it: Windows hands it to the launcher. Before you join, the launcher shows what kind of connection it is. Join by address takes an address ( host:port ) and optionally a guest code, account and password. Note: Peer-to-peer invites, the relay and the community directory are built and tested but switch on later. Until then, add friends' servers by address.

Connection Your IP Notes Through the relay (recommended) Hidden Traffic passes through Open Vanilla's relay, end-to-end encrypted Direct The host sees it Sign-in details between friends travel unencrypted; only join hosts you trust LAN Same network Open Vanilla isn't involved at all The launcher remembers a host's key the first time you join. If it changes, it warns you ("Host key changed … ask them for a new invite link"): someone may be pretending to be them.

Nodes are volunteers' PCs that help carry relay traffic (end-to-end encrypted, never game files). It's optional and in a test round; Open Vanilla's own relay comes first. To volunteer: launcher Host → Become a node (or Esc → Become a Node in game to read about it), set caps for speed and data per day (at the daily cap it pauses until midnight UTC), make sure TCP port 3728 is reachable (UPnP or a forwarded port; carrier-grade NAT can't host), and press Turn on my node . You can list it as anonymous or with a display name. Approved nodes, after three days of steady uptime, get a NODE badge. More

Open Vanilla's network is built so anyone can host a realm and anyone can find and join it safely. It has five parts: Part Runs on What it does The host The host's PC (or Open Vanilla's servers for official realms) Runs the whole world: every player, creature, bot and spell The directory Open Vanilla's server Lists realms by tier, checks they're reachable, tells your launcher how to reach them Relays Open Vanilla's servers Carry traffic for hosts behind home routers, hiding both sides' IP addresses Nodes Volunteers' PCs Extra relays: more connections, attack absorption, shorter routes One sign

t: Why there isn't one giant world
x: A realm's whole world runs in one server program on one machine; on the server Open Vanilla uses, each continent is updated by a single processor core. Relays and nodes add connections , not world power: they can't run part of someone's world, and letting volunteers do that would let them hand out items or read everyone's chat. So Open Vanilla grows in two ways at once: The official realm gets faster: measured tuning, then splitting each continent into regions that run in parallel (the approach Nostalrius used), and copies ("layers") only for launches and big events. Play Solo runs a complete Vanilla realm on your own PC: the SPP Classics server with playerbots , computer-controlled characters who join your group for dungeons and group quests and roam the world. It listens only on your own PC and works offline once it's set up. Good to know Needs Windows 10/11 64-bit, your own Vanilla Client v1.3 (English, build 5875), a few GB of disk (SSD helps), 8 GB+ RAM recommended Internet Only for the first download and updates Characters Stay on your PC: they can't move to or from online realms Players None: no trading, guilds or chat with people Vanilla Remastered

In the launcher, switch Home to SOLO and press PLAY . It downloads the solo server (about 110 MB, then about 700 MB of server files). Both resume if interrupted. The server's setup window opens once: type 1 , wait for the Vanilla menu, then type 0 . PLAY turns ready by itself: READY · SOLO ON THIS PC . Already have SPP Classics? Choose I have SPP Classics… and point the launcher at it.
Press PLAY in Solo mode. The launcher starts the database, login and world servers hidden in the background and logs you in as SOLO / SOLO . Closing the game saves the world and stops the servers.

Playerbots fill the world and will group with you. Ask them to follow, attack or assist in party chat, or let Herald play your own character ( /herald , see In-game features ): Play Solo has Herald's self-bot switched on.

It's your realm: you can change XP rates, add NPCs and give yourself GM powers. The config lives under Realms\Solo\...\mangosd.conf . The easiest way is to ask an AI agent with the starter prompts in Connect an AI , or by hand in Edit your own game . Back up first.

Vanilla Remastered allows 56 race and class pairs, the same as modern retail: Every race can be a Warrior, Hunter, Rogue, Priest, Mage or Warlock. Paladin: Human or Dwarf. Shaman: Orc, Tauren or Troll. Druid: Night Elf, Tauren or Troll. In character creation every class has its own slot; a class your race can't be is greyed out with the reason, and picking it moves you to a race that can. Every class starts with all its class weapon skills; racial weapon bonuses stay with their race. Class quest chains are open to every pair (new hunters, for example, have taming chains in Goldshire and Brill)

Spells learn themselves: every trainer spell and rank is learned when you level up. Trainers will tell you that you already know everything. Faster levels: the XP needed per level is 5–15% lower (levels 1–60 take about 3.7 million XP instead of 4.1 million). Quest and kill XP are unchanged; rested XP builds 25% faster. Free respec and two specs from level 10 (see Talents ). Hunters tame their first pet at 10, as in stock Vanilla.

AoE loot: looting one corpse also gathers from nearby corpses (up to 10 within 30 yards), solo or in free-for-all groups. Quest drops stay on their own corpse; skinning, mining, herbalism and pickpocketing are unchanged. Instant mail between characters on the same account.

You get a Star Pouch every time you gain a level (by mail if your bags are full). Pouches don't stack and sit in the To open lane of your bags. Each holds gold, a potion kit, a scroll and a world-drop green for its level band, with a 25% chance of a second green. Close it and anything left goes into your bags. The realm keeps your achievements, so they survive reinstalls and show on the Armory . Progress you made before achievements launched is granted on your first login after.

Some realms use playerbots: computer-controlled characters. Play Solo is built around them ( chapter 5 ), and the Warfront realm fills battlegrounds with bots during bot-fill hours (you're told when you enter, and bots never count for streaks or bounties). Bots are always the realm's own; Open Vanilla never presents bots as players.

t: Your first login: pick a kit
x: On your first login a window welcomes you and asks you to pick a kit : a level-60 class and spec loadout for your faction with pre-enchanted gear (for example, an Arms Warrior in Field Marshal's plate). Open the window again any time with /wf (or /warfront , /kit ).

Gear picker ( /wf gear ): three tiers, Starter , Tier 2 and Tier 3 . Higher tiers unlock with arena rating or honorable kills. Shop ( /wf shop ): consumables for gold. Shared sets ( /wf sets ): save up to 10 sets and share them; others can vote, and three reports hide a set. Kits, gear and the shop can't be used in combat, while dead, inside an instance or while queued.

Open the arena tab with /arena (or /wf arena ). Level 60 only; the party leader queues the party. Command Queue /arena s2 2v2 Skirmish /arena s3 3v3 Skirmish /arena r2 2v2 Rated /arena r3 3v3 Rated /arena d1 1v1 Duel Ladder /arena leave Leave the queue When the queue pops you get a 60-second preparation countdown, then Fight! Live queue counts (battlegrounds too) refresh every 10 seconds.

Long kill streaks are announced in chat and put a bounty on the player; take them down and you'll see Bounty collected . During bot-fill hours the realm fills battlegrounds with bots; you're told when you enter, and bots never count for streaks or bounties.

Stuck in a wall, dead in a bad spot, talents broken? Open a ticket in game: Help → Talk to a GM . Use the bug-reports forum on Discord: what happened, what you expected, the steps to make it happen again, and a screenshot if you can. Staff can turn a good report straight into a tracked issue. Security problems go privately instead: see security.html .

In game: right-click their name → Report . The report includes the chat around it, so staff see context. On the website: realms, Workshop addons and streams have a report option. Herald sorts reports and suggests an action; humans decide (dismiss, warn, mute, kick, ban). The only things Herald does by itself are hiding repeated spam and a 10-minute mute for hard spam or gold selling, and both can be undone. Appeal with /appeal <text> in game or a DM to Herald.

Open Vanilla is free and run by volunteers. Tips keep it that way. Where: ko-fi.com/orionvanilla (card or PayPal, once or monthly), also linked from Support the realm on the site and in the launcher. x: The Model Porter turns a modern model into one the Vanilla client can show, and adds it to your realm as a creature or rideable mount. Run Model_Porter.bat ; it opens http://127.0.0.1:8765 . The Vanilla Remastered windows, icons and frames are drawn by scripts in tools/ ( gen_*_art.py , sharing tools/artkit.py ). Each writes a .tga for the Vanilla client and a .blp for the browser client; sizes must be powers of two. tools/png_to_blp.py converts your own PNGs.

The Workshop can host copies only under: MIT, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0, LGPL-2.1, LGPL-3.0, MPL-2.0, Unlicense, CC0-1.0. It's yours to share. You wrote it, or its licence allows sharing and you credit the author. Screenshots and a one-line summary ready. An AI agent can draft the list

On the Workshop page , Share an addon (signed in): Field Limit Addon name 48 characters One line 280 characters Licence One from the list above Source link Optional, https Zip The addon folder with its .toc and licence, up to 10 MB Tick I wrote this addon, or its licence lets anyone share it, and the licence file is in the zip , and send. You'll see "Upload #n is in the review queue". You can upload five a day, with at most five waiting. Note: Uploads open with the realm update that adds them. Until then, use a catalogue entry .

Every upload is scanned in the fake Vanilla client before a person looks at it. The scanner flags anything that sends chat when it loads or on a timer, reads other addons' saved data, uses os or io , moves gold or items, or runs arbitrary code. Anything serious holds the upload for a moderator. Uploads are never served to players until a moderator approves them; approved ones become catalogue entries.

The Workshop's source is one file per addon in workshop/catalog/<id>.yml in the repo. Adding yours by pull request: id: my-theme # lowercase, digits, dashes; 2-48 characters name: MyTheme author: You summary: A dark, minimal skin for the Vanilla Remastered windows. description: | What it does, how to open it (/mytheme), what to expect. category: interface # interface, unitframes, combat, raid, quests, bags, maps, # social, economy, professions, macros, tooltips, utility, classicplus tags: [theme, minimal] license: MIT rehost: true source_url: https://github.com/you/MyTheme homepage: https://gi
Add one of these topics to your GitHub repo: wow-vanilla-addon , vanilla-wow-addon or turtle-wow . The indexer finds tagged repos, and a person reviews each before it's listed.

t: Port an open addon into Vanilla Remastered
x: Vanilla Remastered addons get the suite's settings window and look. To wrap an openly licensed addon: python3 tools/workshop_port.py path\to\SomeAddon --license MIT --name SomeAddonPlus --author "You" --source https://... It writes workshop/ports/<Folder>Plus/ (a .toc , a Lua file and PORT_NOTES.txt ), refuses addons without an allowed licence, and never publishes anything by itself. Test it in the sim and the game, then upload it.

A collection is a curated list of addons for a play style (raiders, roleplayers...), installed with one click. They live in workshop/collections/<id>.yml : id , name , curator , summary , description , banner and addons: [ids] . Send one by pull request.
Signed-in players can rate and review addons on each addon's page. Moderators can hide a review's text if it breaks the rules. Install counts are anonymous.

t: List a fork, repo or project
x: Forks of Open Vanilla, other clients, server projects, repacks and games built on the same tech go in the Projects directory ( www/community/directory.json ). Each gets a page at project.html#<id> and a spot in the launcher's Workshop → Projects tab. To be listed, open an issue with the name, link, a short description, the credits and a screenshot. Fork the repo on GitHub ( orionopenwow/OpenVanilla ) or clone it to another host. Keep the credits. Open Vanilla is built on benilla (MIT / Apache-2.0); keep its licence files and credit line. Keep Blizzard's files out. The repo's checks refuse them, and so should your fork: players bring their own Vanilla Client v1.3. Rename it. Use your own name and art; don't present your fork as the official Open Vanilla. Point it at your own realm. Realm addresses live in the launcher's defaults and the site's config; your fork's players should never sign in to a realm you don't run. List it in the Projec

Report bugs in the Discord's bug-reports forum or as GitHub issues , with your logs ( Logs\ in the launcher's data folder). Make addons and publish them . Stream and make videos : link your channel . Host a realm or run a node . Fix the manual (next). Send code : see below.

This manual is plain text in the repo: one Markdown file per chapter in docs/manual/ . To fix or add something: Edit the chapter's .md file. Sections are ## Heading {#link-id} ; keep existing ids so links keep working. Build it: python tools/build_manual.py --check . It writes the pages to www/manual/ and fails if any link or anchor is broken. Send it as a pull request, or describe the change in an issue. An AI agent with the workspace kit can do this for you: "Read CLAUDE.md. In docs/manual/, add a section about <topic> to the right chapter, then run the build with --check."

py -3 devkit\check.py # repo checks (CI runs --strict) lua5.1 devkit/sim/run_tests.lua # addon tests python devkit/db/test_sql.py --local # realm database changes py -3 -m pytest tests # launcher, site, bot, tools When you fix a bug, add a test that would have caught it: addon bugs in devkit/sim/tests/<addon>.lua , server or SQL bugs in devkit/db/test_sql.py or a Herald Lite scenario.

A release is playtested on staging, gets a ## New in X.Y.Z section in CHANGELOG.md , and is tagged by the maintainer. The build server makes the installer, the zip, their checksums and a signed update manifest; launchers pick it up by themselves.

No Blizzard files, ever: checks refuse MPQs, DBCs and stock interface files. No secrets in commits: tokens, keys and passwords stay in .env files that git ignores. Keep it free: nothing that sells power, items or game time.
Launcher: Settings → Folders → Open logs . The files that matter are launcher.log , update.log and web-backend.log . Attach them to a bug report (they don't contain your password).
